Cartesian coordinates for a population pyramid

Source: R/coord-pyramid.R
coord_pyramid.Rd

coord_pyramid() is a Cartesian coordinate system for horizontal pyramids drawn with position_pyramid(). It labels the value axis without the minus sign on the left side, extends the value axis equally far on both sides of zero, and places the age axis on the left, on the right, on both sides or in the centre of the pyramid, optionally in a gap between the two sides.

Usage

coord_pyramid(
  age_axis = c("left", "right", "both", "centre", "none"),
  left = NULL,
  gap = NULL,
  symmetric = TRUE,
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  expand = TRUE,
  clip = "on"
)

Arguments

age_axis

Where to draw the age axis: "left", "right", "both", "centre" (between the two sides, see Age axis below) or "none". "center" is accepted as well.

left

The value of the side variable drawn on the left, such as "Female", for every layer drawn with position_pyramid(). A layer can override it with position_pyramid(left = ...). Defaults to the first level when the side variable is a factor, and to the first value in sorted order otherwise. The legend keeps its own order; set it with, for example, scale_fill_discrete(breaks = c("Female", "Male")).

gap

The width of an empty strip between the two sides, as a proportion of the panel width. Defaults to 0.12 when age_axis is "centre", which leaves room for the age labels, and to 0 otherwise.

symmetric

If TRUE, the value axis extends equally far on both sides of zero, so the two sides share one scale. Ignored when xlim is set.

xlim, ylim

Limits for the x and y axes.

expand

If TRUE, the default, adds a small expansion factor to the limits to ensure that data and axes don't overlap. If FALSE, limits are taken exactly from the data or xlim/ylim. Giving a logical vector will separately control the expansion for the four directions (top, left, bottom and right). The expand argument will be recycled to length 4 if necessary. Alternatively, can be a named logical vector to control a single direction, e.g. expand = c(bottom = FALSE).

clip

Should drawing be clipped to the extent of the plot panel? A setting of "on" (the default) means yes, and a setting of "off" means no. In most cases, the default of "on" should not be changed, as setting clip = "off" can cause unexpected results. It allows drawing of data points anywhere on the plot, including in the plot margins. If limits are set via xlim and ylim and some data points fall outside those limits, then those data points may show up in places such as the axes, the legend, the plot title, or the plot margins.

Value

A ggproto object of class CoordPyramid.

Value axis

Only the labels lose their sign. The data and the scale keep the signed values that position_pyramid() produces, so breaks, limits and reference lines on the left side are still given as negative numbers. Any labels given to ggplot2::scale_x_continuous() apply to the absolute values, for example labels = scales::label_percent(). With a gap, a break at zero is drawn on both inner edges, so a gap narrower than two zero labels makes them overlap. The value axis must be linear, and a secondary value axis keeps its signs.

Age axis

"left" and "right" move the age scale to that side together with its title, and "both" duplicates it on the right, as scale_y_discrete(sec.axis = dup_axis()) would. "centre" draws the age labels inside the panel, above the layers and in the middle of the gap, styled by the axis.text.y.left theme element. If the labels are wider than the gap, increase gap.

See also

position_pyramid(), which mirrors the left side.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

pop <- data.frame(
  age = factor(rep(c("0-19", "20-39", "40-59", "60+"), 2)),
  sex = factor(rep(c("Male", "Female"), each = 4), c("Male", "Female")),
  n = c(220, 200, 160, 90, 210, 205, 170, 120)
)
p <- ggplot(pop, aes(x = n, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_pyramid()

p + coord_pyramid()


# Women on the left
p + coord_pyramid(left = "Female")


# Age labels in a gap between the two sides
p + coord_pyramid(age_axis = "centre")


# Age labels on both sides, with a narrow gap
p + coord_pyramid(age_axis = "both", gap = 0.08)
